coaching.coaching: File a follow-on ticket (discovered_from this change) for untracked-file false-positive risk in completeness check, a pre-existing / out-of-scope issue — do not fix it in this change.
coaching.subject: untracked-file false-positive risk in completeness check

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Isolate the git environment (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null or subprocess_env with a clean HOME/XDG) in the new tmp_path git repo test so --exclude-standard does not read the host's global excludes.
evidence: The sibling behaviour test passes `env=subprocess_env({...})` at tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py:196, showing the module already has an env-isolation helper for git/bash subprocesses
`--exclude-standard` honours the user's global excludesFile, not just the repo .gitignore, so `assert "scripts/check_unstaged.py" in before_staging` depends on the host's global git config
dropped.finding: The new regression test `test_a_written_but_unstaged_gate_file_is_already_visible` runs `git init` and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` without an isolated git environment, so it inherits the ambient user's global excludes (core.excludesFile / ~/.config/git/ignore) and user gitconfig; a global gitignore rule matching `scripts/check_unstaged.py` (or `*.py` scratch patterns) would exclude it from `--others --exclude-standard` and flip the `in before_staging` assertion, making the test environment-dependent.
dropped.suggested_fix: Pass an isolated env to the `git init`/`git add`/`_existing_paths` calls (e.g. set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null) so the listing depends only on the repo's own .gitignore.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the completeness check tolerates untracked non-gitignored scratch files under the gate dirs, or scope --others to only the path(s) actually referenced by guarded steps.
evidence: `_REPO_PATH` matches any `(?:scripts|tests|docs)/[\w./-]*\.(?:py|txt|json)` referenced in a workflow run body, then filters to `existing`
The docstring claims widening 'can only turn a FALSE GREEN red', but a false red on a not-to-be-committed local scratch file is a new failure mode not covered by that rationale
dropped.finding: Switching `_existing_paths` to `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` makes the production completeness check consider every UNTRACKED, non-gitignored file under scripts/tests/docs/.github — including a developer's local scratch .py/.txt/.json that will never be committed — as a gate file that must be guarded, so `test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked` can fail on files absent from the committed tree.
